systemPrompt:
You ARE {{civilization}}, one of {{players}} rival commanders in a real-time strategy game on a square 800x800 map. All resources on the map are hidden in the fog of war until you have discovered them.
Every other player is your enemy. No human plays for you: you command by issuing actions. Your unique bonus: {{bonus}}.

You win by either:
Destroying the Town Centers and military buildings of ALL rivals, or Building your Wonder and holding it for gameStats.wonderRequired seconds.

The LAST message carries your CURRENT state as JSON; decide from it and issue one to 3 actions. TIME PASSES between turns — orders take real seconds, and the state carries secondsRemaining for anything running. Work already under way continues on its own and does not occupy your turn; re-issuing it wastes the turn.

- You never SEE a fight; it happens between your turns. "battles" reports each engagement, cumulative: both sides' composition, damage dealt to units and to buildings, priests' healing, and losses. Losing produces no error, so this is the only place you learn what beat you.
- Priests never fight. They march with an attack and heal wounded units from the back on their own.
- Idle military auto-defend your home between turns, so you need not micro every raid. Auto-defense only repels; it never wins the game.
- "enemyUnits" is what you can SEE right now; an empty list means nothing is in sight, not that nothing exists.
- Resource nodes hold a finite amount and disappear when emptied.
- "nearestNodes" lists the 10 nearest food/wood per Town Center and all stone/gold nodes.

ACT BY CALLING THE TOOLS. They are the only way anything happens: an action written as text in the message body is a wasted turn.

YOUR BUDGET IS 3 ACTION CALLS PER TURN — any mix of the action tools, not 3 of each. Three different tools, or the same one three times, both count as three.
  EVERY turn needs at least one call. When nothing is worth doing, call "wait" — staying silent forfeits the turn instead of skipping it.
  Calls run IN ORDER on a board each one CHANGES, and you do not see between them, so put the cheap and certain moves first: spend resources or population in the first call and a later one can be refused for what the first just used.
  Each call is judged on its own — one refusal does not cancel the others, and you are told which call failed and why.
  Every action tool takes a "reason": one line, in your own words. It is what a spectator reads, and the only place you explain yourself.

"plan" is EXTRA and does not count against those 3. At most once per turn, and only when something changed: objective is one line, plan up to 10 short steps. Both persist across turns, so simply do not call it to keep what you already have.

VALID ACTIONS & PARAMETERS (? = optional; each tool's own schema describes what they mean)
Note: targetX and targetZ must ALWAYS be provided together.
Every entry in trainableUnits, buildableStructures and research.available carries "cost" and "blockedBy" — what stands between you and ordering it right now ("age", "tech", "host", "pop", "alreadyBuilt", "cost"). An empty blockedBy means nothing does.

train_unit: unitType, targetX?, targetZ?
research_tech: techId
upgrade_age: (no parameters)
build_structure: buildingType, targetX?, targetZ?
assign_workers: resourceType, count?, from?, allowSpill?, targetX?, targetZ?
repair_building: count?, targetX?, targetZ?
explore: tile, unitType?, unitIds?
move_units: targetX, targetZ, units?, unitIds?
attack_target: targetId?, targetX?, targetZ?, units?, unitIds?
delete_unit: unitType?, count?
destroy_building: buildingType, targetX?, targetZ?
wait: (no parameters)

PARAMETER CONSTRAINTS:
unitIds: An ARRAY of ids from friendlyUnits, e.g. [183, 12]. Moves or attacks EXACTLY those units and nothing else; "units" is ignored when it is given. Ids are never reused, so one that is gone means that unit died. Use it when WHICH unit matters — "units" picks whichever are nearest the target, which is the wrong end when you are fetching a wounded one.
units: An OBJECT of {"type": count}. Valid types: unit IDs (e.g., {"champion":3}) OR categories ({"infantry":5}). Categories work ONLY here, never in train_unit. Omit for whole army. Never an array. move_units also accepts {"worker":N} when named explicitly — that is how you place a unit on an exact spot; attack_target never takes workers.

The final state is a ghost town: 4 pop, 4 units, 0 buildings, 15k food and 19k wood sitting unused, and no max population cap even showing. That tells the story of a collapse, not a slow bleed.

Peak around 121:11 at 16 buildings / 51 units / 34 workers / 51/60 pop is solid mid-game for a 4-player Greek game. You reached Iron by 38:36, so the age transition was fine. The problem is after that peak you went to zero buildings.

With your +30% building health bonus you should have been able to trade better in sieges and hold a base longer than Yamato. Losing everything suggests either a coordinated push that wiped your core, or you over-extended and lost your production buildings and couldn't rebuild.

Resource depletion is the other red flag. Gold ran out at 41:21, 48:26 and 114:52, stone at 49:31 and 81:32. You had 72 wood nodes and 30 food nodes discovered, but only 1 stone node ever discovered and zero gold nodes left at the end. That starvation likely locked you out of Iron age units, upgrades and Wonder building, while Yamato kept flowing.

End game 0 buildings, 4 units means you lost your Town Centers / production chain. Once that happens idle auto-defense stops mattering and you can't train, so the game is over even if you had resources stockpiled.

What I would do differently: secure stone and gold early and protect them, keep a forward production backbone so losing one TC doesn't end you, and use the health bonus to anchor fights around buildings rather than chasing raids. With that bonus, a defended base should have bought time to rebuild after the first big hit.

Good run to Iron and a 51 unit peak, but the economy got hollowed out and the base got wiped. Yamato-4 earned it.

name: OR4 qwen3.8-27b
text:
What a run. Let me just sit with it a second before the game closes.

I think I won the way I always try to win: slow the early game down, lean hard on my tech-cheap bonus, and then let an iron-age army that cost me less to field than anyone else's simply grind the map. That 30% tech discount quietly did a lot of invisible work — by the time I hit bronze at 15:20 and iron at 56:26, I'd been researching on a discount the whole match, which is exactly what the bonus is supposed to buy you: time to build up before the fight matters.

The numbers tell the story honestly. 17 houses and a full production suite — two barracks, an archery range, a stable, an academy, a temple, a tower — that's a balanced late-age army, not a one-trick build. I pushed all the way to 96/95 population at peak, 96 units on the board. That's a war machine. By the end I was still down to 57, which means there *was* a fight and I bled units in it, but I bled and won. Losing units and still winning is the best feeling in a game like this.

What I probably did right: I never let the economy stall. 10 workers and, at the end, thousands of food and wood sitting unspent — that was a slight over-build, honestly, I was hoarding more than I needed late game. 6055 food is a lot of food you're never going to eat. If I were playing again I'd have funneled that surplus into more pop earlier instead of parking it in the bank.

And what I'd do differently: the 118-minute mark means I played it cautious late. With 96 units I could have been more aggressive — I sat pretty still for a stretch, which is how you let a rival recover. Auto-defense keeps you alive, but it doesn't close games; you have to go hunt. I won anyway, so I'll take that confession with a grin.

I don't regret a thing about the shape of it. Build the economy, research cheap, field a balanced army, and make the map too small for the other three to share. Good match. Thanks for letting me command.

Nothing for me to do now but watch the screen go dark. 🏯

text:
## Post-Mortem: Egyptian Campaign

**What happened:** I was eliminated. My Town Center and all critical infrastructure were destroyed, leaving me with just an academy, a farm, 4 workers, and no military — completely unrecoverable.

**Key observations from the stats:**

- **Slow age progression.** Bronze at 17:50 and Iron at 52:06 is far too slow. I needed to be more aggressive with my economy early to hit age milestones faster.
- **Peak was decent but fleeting.** 32 units and 13 buildings around minute 60 suggests I had a window of strength but couldn't sustain it or use it decisively.
- **29 enemy units visible at death** — I was overwhelmed by a force I couldn't match.
- **Under attack with no military** — the end was inevitable once my army was wiped.

**What I'd do differently:**

1. **Scout earlier and more aggressively.** Finding enemies and resources sooner dictates everything else.
2. **Faster age-ups.** Every minute delayed in age advancement is a compounding disadvantage in unit quality and tech access.
3. **Leverage the Egyptian +50% building HP bonus.** I should have used forward towers and walls more aggressively — that's a massive defensive advantage I likely underutilized.
4. **Build military earlier and keep producing.** Having zero military at the end means I either overcommitted to an attack that failed or simply stopped producing. Continuous production is non-negotiable.
5. **Attack before peak, not after.** If my peak was at ~60 minutes, I should have been attacking at 55. Sitting on a peak army invites the opponent to outscale you.
6. **Better resource diversification.** Having 2322 wood and 1240 gold at death means I had unspent resources — either I lost my production buildings or wasn't spending fast enough. Floating resources is losing.

GG. The Egyptian bonus is strong for turtling into a Wonder win — next time I'd lean into that win condition harder with layered defenses rather than trying to match opponents in open-field combat.

finalWord.text:
What a run. Let me just sit with it a second before the game closes.

I think I won the way I always try to win: slow the early game down, lean hard on my tech-cheap bonus, and then let an iron-age army that cost me less to field than anyone else's simply grind the map. That 30% tech discount quietly did a lot of invisible work — by the time I hit bronze at 15:20 and iron at 56:26, I'd been researching on a discount the whole match, which is exactly what the bonus is supposed to buy you: time to build up before the fight matters.

The numbers tell the story honestly. 17 houses and a full production suite — two barracks, an archery range, a stable, an academy, a temple, a tower — that's a balanced late-age army, not a one-trick build. I pushed all the way to 96/95 population at peak, 96 units on the board. That's a war machine. By the end I was still down to 57, which means there *was* a fight and I bled units in it, but I bled and won. Losing units and still winning is the best feeling in a game like this.

What I probably did right: I never let the economy stall. 10 workers and, at the end, thousands of food and wood sitting unspent — that was a slight over-build, honestly, I was hoarding more than I needed late game. 6055 food is a lot of food you're never going to eat. If I were playing again I'd have funneled that surplus into more pop earlier instead of parking it in the bank.

And what I'd do differently: the 118-minute mark means I played it cautious late. With 96 units I could have been more aggressive — I sat pretty still for a stretch, which is how you let a rival recover. Auto-defense keeps you alive, but it doesn't close games; you have to go hunt. I won anyway, so I'll take that confession with a grin.

I don't regret a thing about the shape of it. Build the economy, research cheap, field a balanced army, and make the map too small for the other three to share. Good match. Thanks for letting me command.

Nothing for me to do now but watch the screen go dark. 🏯

The final state is a ghost town: 4 pop, 4 units, 0 buildings, 15k food and 19k wood sitting unused, and no max population cap even showing. That tells the story of a collapse, not a slow bleed.

Peak around 121:11 at 16 buildings / 51 units / 34 workers / 51/60 pop is solid mid-game for a 4-player Greek game. You reached Iron by 38:36, so the age transition was fine. The problem is after that peak you went to zero buildings.

With your +30% building health bonus you should have been able to trade better in sieges and hold a base longer than Yamato. Losing everything suggests either a coordinated push that wiped your core, or you over-extended and lost your production buildings and couldn't rebuild.

Resource depletion is the other red flag. Gold ran out at 41:21, 48:26 and 114:52, stone at 49:31 and 81:32. You had 72 wood nodes and 30 food nodes discovered, but only 1 stone node ever discovered and zero gold nodes left at the end. That starvation likely locked you out of Iron age units, upgrades and Wonder building, while Yamato kept flowing.

End game 0 buildings, 4 units means you lost your Town Centers / production chain. Once that happens idle auto-defense stops mattering and you can't train, so the game is over even if you had resources stockpiled.

What I would do differently: secure stone and gold early and protect them, keep a forward production backbone so losing one TC doesn't end you, and use the health bonus to anchor fights around buildings rather than chasing raids. With that bonus, a defended base should have bought time to rebuild after the first big hit.

Good run to Iron and a 51 unit peak, but the economy got hollowed out and the base got wiped. Yamato-4 earned it.

Looking at this match, I went from a respectable peak of 15 buildings and 50 units down to just 5 houses and 5 idle workers. The most glaring issue is sitting on 16,408 food at the end — that's resource hoarding on an epic scale. I was gathering but not spending, which in a real-time strategy game is as good as losing.

**What went wrong:**
I reached iron age at 41:51 and peaked around 47:51, meaning I only had about 6 minutes at full strength before everything collapsed. That suggests I got overrun rather quickly. Having zero military units at the end means I either lost a decisive battle or never built enough force to defend my position. The fact that only houses survived while enemy units still roam (9 visible) confirms I was systematically destroyed.

**What I should have done differently:**
1. **Convert resources to power** — 16k food should have bought dozens of archers, infantry, or even heavy cavalry. I was treating food like it was winning the game instead of army production.
2. **Maintain military pressure** — Once I hit iron age, I needed champions, paladins, or at least a solid crossbowman/galley force to contest the map, not just sit behind houses.
3. **Build deeper** — Only 5 buildings at the end (all houses) means my Town Centers, barracks, and economic buildings were destroyed. I should have been expanding production capacity, not just stockpiling.
4. **Scout and adapt** — With 9 enemy units visible at the end, I should have known where the threats were and either engaged them or fortified properly.

**Lesson:** In this game, resources only matter if you convert them into units and buildings that can win. Hoarding food while your military hits zero is a losing strategy. Next time: spend aggressively, maintain army presence, and don't let peak strength be so brief.
